 J U D G M E N T

This petition under Section 22 of Workmen Compensation Act1953 is filed by Mohamed Irfan seeking compensation of .40,00,000/ from the Respondents as he sustained injuries in road traffic accident during the employment under the first Respondent.
2. Brief facts of the case are as under:

The Petitioner was working under Respondent No.1 as a driver of his Goods carrier vehicle bearing No.KA01AK2453 (herein after called as offending vehicle) on a monthly salary of .10,000/ and bata of .400/ per day.

On 01052019 about 1.30 a.m. the Petitioner was driving the said goods carrier during the course of employment from Airport towards Market side, reached opposite of Prolife hospital,
Byatarayanapura flyover, BB Road, Bengaluru, one vegetable bag was fell from his vehicle, it was informed by on going vehicle passers and as such, Petitioner stopped his vehicle and loading the vegetable bag inside the vehicle, meanwhile an unknown vehicle hit against the Petitioner.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner sustained severe injuries all over the body.

Immediately, he was taken to Bowring Hospital, wherein first aid was taken, then shifted to Sanjaygandhi hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an inpatient for 16 days and underwent 5 surgeries and his left leg above knee was amputed.
He has spent .4,00,000/ towards treatment and other expenses.
Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently handicap, lost his earning capacity and income.
Due to which, he has facing financial problems, himself and his family members were depending on others for their livelihood.

The Hebbal Traffic police have registered a criminal case in Crime No.55/2019 under section 279,
338 of IPC.

It is stated that the accident occurred during the course of employment under the Respondent No.1 and hence he has sought for compensation from the Respondent No.1 being the owner and Respondent No.2 as Insurer of the Respondent No.1 vehicle mentioned above.
3.
In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statement.
4. The Respondent No.1(a)has filed his written statement stating that he is the son and LR of deceased Respondent No.1, who died on 19042021.

He has admitted that his father was the RC owner of offending vehicle and the same was insured with Respondent No.2 and it was valid as on the date of accident and as such it is liable to pay compensation.
He admitted the occurrence of accident, involvement of offending vehicle and manner of accident.
He denied that the Petitioner has approached the Respondent No.1/his father seeking compensation.

Further, he has admitted that the Petitioner was working under deceased Respondent No.1 as a driver and drawing salary of Mohamed Irfan vs Nawab Baig on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152909388/
2 .15,000/p.m. and bata of .400/ per day.
The compensation claimed by the Petitioner is exaggerated.
Further, the policy covers all the risks including the injury/death of the driver/3rd party in the use of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.2 has to indemnify the liability.
Hence this Respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.
5. Respondent No.2  Insurance company filed its written statement by denying the petition averments.
It has denied the employer and employee relationship between the 1st Respondent and the Petitioner.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and also the if the relationship of employer and employee is proved.
It has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL and it had no valid FC and permit.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings following issues are framed by the court.
1.Whether the Petitioner  proves that there is employee and employer relationship between him and the first Respondent?

2. Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries during the course of employment in an accident occurred on 0105 2019 while he was driving the Goods Carrier bearing No.KA01 AK 2453 belonging to 1st Respondent?
3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation?

If so what is the quantum and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
7.
Petitioner examined himself as PW1 and the doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 18 respectively.

The insurance company has examined the IO as RW1 and and the Respondent No.1(a) is examined as RW2 and got marked 3 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3.
8.
After hearing the arguments and by considering available materials and evidence on record I have answered the above Issues as under.
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4: As per the final order, for the following:

sentences.text: 3 9. Issue No.1:
The Petitioner claims that he is an employee under Respondent No.1 Nawab Baig.
Respondent No.1(a) also admits that the Petitioner is working as a driver under his father.
Respondent No.2 insurance company denied the relationship of employee and employer between the Petitioner and Respondent No.1.

So far as his relationship is concerned, Respondent No.1(a)
admits in his written statement as well as in his evidence that Petitioner was under employment with his father.

Though there are no documentary evidence to show that the Petitioner was employee under Respondent No.1, the admission by Respondent No.1(a) and his evidence clearly indicates that the Petitioner was working under Respondent No.1 as driver.
Respondent No.1(a)/ RW2 said that his father had appointed Petitioner as driver and was paying salary of .15,000/ p.m. with daily bata of .400/.
The cross examination of RW2 could not disprove his evidence.
10. Petitioner has produced his DL at Ex.P.6 which shows he has DL to drive LMV, LMV Transport and 3WGV, MCWG.
He has DL to drive transport motor vehicle since 2005 and he appears to be a driver by profession.
Hence, by considering all the evidences and materials on record and by taking into consideration of evidence of RW2, I hold that petitioner was an employee under Respondent No.1 as a driver.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
11.Issue No.2:
The next relevant question is whether the accident has taken place during the course of employment?
The accident has taken place on 01052019 when the Petitioner was driving the Goods carrier bearing No.KA01AK2453 belonging to Respondent No.1.
Petitioner was driving the said vehicle along with vegetable bags.
He had got down from the vehicle after noticing that a vegetable bad had fallen on the road which was informed by some passe.
When he was putting the bag into his vehicle and unknown vehicle got hit him.
12. Counsel for Respondent No.2 denied the occurrence of accident and the manner as stated by the petitioner.
It is contended that the version of the petitioner cannot be believed for the reason that the petitioner has not proved that he was there at the spot at the time of accident.

It is also disputed by the respondent No.2 that a severely injured person cannot be there at the spot for 45 minutes by calling his brother over phone and waiting for him at the place of accident itself.
There is nothing to disbelieve with this fact since it is obvious that a person who gets injured will call his friends or relatives seeking help immediately.
Since it was a Hebbal Fly over one may get time to reach the spot.
A person having severally injured may not be able to move or drive.
He had no other option than waiting his brother till he comes to the spot since it was 1.30 a.m. and hardly he could find any public who may help.

13. Respondent - Insurance company further argued that the place of accident is wrongly mentioned and alleged that the goods vehicle was not at all at the place of accident at that time and it is falsely implicated.
Insurance company examined the IO as RW1 and treated him hostile.
IO has stated that he had verified at the toll and examined the witnesses and found that Scorpio vehicle had hit the petitioner and its number could not be traced.

He has stated that he did not collect the GPS Mohamed Irfan vs Nawab Baig on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152909388/
4 details of the petitioner's vehicle.

sentences.text: 14. The initial medical records of the petitioner shows that he got admitted with a history of RTA and when he was a pedestrian he was hit by a Car.

Based on this entry at Ex.P.12 & 17 Insurance company argued that the petitioner was not a driver and he has sustained injuries while he was walking and the insured vehicle was falsely implicated in this case.
It is suggested that the Petitioner has sustained injuries somewhere else and falsely claimed that it has occurred during the course of employment.
For this contention, petitioner has already explained that he was bringing vegetables from the Airport and he had got down from the vehicle to load the fallen bag.
For this reason, in the history it might have been mentioned that he was walking on the road or a pedestrian.
Hence, this contention of the respondent No.2 is also not accepted.
RW/IO has stated that he did not gave any notice to the respondent No.1 U/s.133 of MV Act.
This could be a lapse on the part of IO and the petitioner cannot be disbelieved only for this reason.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.3:
The wound certificate Ex.P6 reveals that the Petitioner has sustained Left Proximal 1/3rd both bone leg fracture vascular injury at popliteal artery open type 2 wound.
According to the doctor, the above said injuries are grievous in nature.
The discharge summary Ex.P.12 shows that he has taken treatment as an inpatient at Sanjaygandhi Hospital, Bengaluru for a period of 16 days and undergone 5 surgeries.
16. Dr.Avinash Prarthasarathy, who is Professor of Orthopedics has been examined as PW2.
He has stated in his evidence that the Petitioner was treated with emergency surgery - External fixation for left proximal tibia with vascular repair.
Further PW2 has stated that Petitioner also underwent 2 more surgeries, Reexploration of venous graft and let leg above knee amputation was done.

On 02082021 PW2 has examined the Petitioner for assessment of disability and stated that the Petitioner is having difficulty in squatting, kneeling and sitting cross legged, tenderness over mid 1/3 left femur/amputated stump, antalgic gait in his left lower limb, arc movement of left hip flexion, rotation and abduction restricted by 30 degree each and he had pain in left thigh and restricted ROM in the left hip joint and difficulty in doing his daily activities.
With these observations, PW2 has assessed the whole body disability at 43%.

Along with his evidence PW2 has produced OPD card, inpatient record and X ray at Ex.P.16 to 18.
17.
In the crossexamination PW2 doctor has stated that he has not treated the petitioner and the amputation is for 8 inches above the knee.

He assessed only physical disability and except left leg,
no other parts of the body are injured.
He has taken 50% of the limb disability to the whole body.
The petitioner counsel argued that the petitioner is unable to continue his avocation as a driver and it is 100% functional disability.
The counsel for Insurance company has argued that 100% functional disability cannot be considered under ECA.

Respondent No.2 relied on the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.8510/2022 in the case of Sidram Vs. The Divisional Manager,
United India Insurance Co.Ltd., and argued that The Tribunal shall keep in view the First Schedule to the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 which gives some indication about the extent of permanent disability in different types of injuries, in the case of workmen.

sentences.text: Considering all these facts and based on First Schedule of the Workmen Compensation Act, I am of the opinion that the 100% disability argued by the petitioner is exonerated.
Taking note of the nature of the injury and the duration of the treatment, this Tribunal is of the view that earning capacity of the Petitioner is impaired to the extent of 80%.
Hence, the functional disability of the Petitioner is taken to the extent of 80%.

19. Though Petitioner says that he was earning .15,000/p.m. and daily bata of .400/ per day,
there are no documents produced.
Even the Respondent No.1(a) owner has also not produced any documents.
Considering that he is a driver income of the Petitioner is taken as .15,000/p.m.
By considering the DL of the Petitioner, which shows his dater of birth as 04031980 and hence his age is considered as 39 yea.
Then, the relevant factor is 186.90.

As per Section 4 of the Employee's Compensation Act, Where permanent disability results from injury, an amount equal to 60% of the monthly wages of the injured to be taken Thus, 60% of .15,000/ will come to .9,000/ and 80%
of the disability for that amount comes to .7,200/.

If this amount is multiplied by factor 186.90,
the total amount will be .13,45,680/.
Therefore, Petitioner is entitled for the said sum towards loss of income due to permanent disability.
20. The Petitioner has produced medical bills amounting to .70,000/ as per Ex.P13.
He has not produced any bills pertaining to treatment and medicines and the bills at Ex.P.13 is for Left Transfemural Prosthesis.
There is no serious dispute with regard to this bill by Respondent.

Hence,
in total .70,000/ is awarded under the head of medical expenses.

21. For future medical expenses, the doctor has stated in his evidence that the Petitioner has to undergo A/K total contact suction prosthesis (artificial limb) and it would improve his quality of life,
which would cost approximately .1,00,000/.

The Petitioner has produced Ex.P.14, which shows that using imported Dynamic motion foot with pneumatic knee joint (3R78) and other accessories,
the total cost of the prosthesis will be .2,50,000/.
Petitioner has already purchased one prosthesis and he may require to change the same after few yea.

By considering all these evidence it would be reasonable to award .1,00,000/ towards future medical expenses/Prosthesis.
22.

In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioner under various headings is as follows :
Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount No.
1. Loss of Income .13,45,680/.
2. Medical Expenses . 70,000/
3. Future Medical Expenses .1,00,000/ Total .15,15,680/
23.
Thus, the Petitioner is entitled for .13,45,680/.

In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in AIR 2014 SUPREME COURT 1393 (Saberabibi Yakubbhai Saikh vs. National insurance Co Ltd., and others), the rate of interest has to be 12% p.a. and it should be awarded from Mohamed Irfan vs Nawab Baig on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152909388/
6 the date of accident.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of accident till realisation.
24. As it is already held that the accident has occurred during the course of employment.
The Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation with interest at 12% p.a.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
25. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Claim petition filed under Section 22 of Employees Compensation Act 1923 is allowed.
The Petitioner is awarded with the compensation of .15,15,680/. with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. (Excluding for future medical expenses) from the date of accident till its realization.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
The Respondent No.2 - insurance company shall pay the compensation amount within three months from the date of this order.

After the deposit, 75% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationaized bank of petitioner's choice and remaining amount with interest shall be released to him through Epayment on proper verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
The Respondent No.2 - insurance company shall pay the compensation amount within three months from the date of this order.

After the deposit, 75% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationaized bank of petitioner's choice and remaining amount with interest shall be released to him through Epayment on proper verification.
